walkthroughs.body_html:
[Cu(H2O)6]^2+ + 4NH3 (after deprotonation) -> [Cu(NH3)4(H2O)2]^2+ (deep blue). 6-coord retained.

[Cu(H2O)6]^2+ + 4Cl- -> [CuCl4]^2- (yellow). Coordination drops from 6 to 4 (larger Cl-, geometry change).

Replacing 6 H2O with 3 bidentate ligands releases 6 H2O molecules but uses 3 new ligands -> entropy rises.

ΔG more negative due to +ΔS, so chelated complex more stable. EDTA traps metal in single 6-coord chelate.

Fe^2+ in haemoglobin reversibly binds O2. CO binds ~200x more strongly than O2 -> dangerous as it does not release.

This is a ligand substitution: O2 displaced by CO. CN- also strongly binds, poisoning cytochromes.
